sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2021 rebound came from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, mostly from the Concho acquisition [P51].
FY2023 revenue fell 20.5% on lower realized commodity prices across all products, partly offset by higher sales volumes [F8][D274][P47].
The table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported, so growth rates mixing recast and first-reported years compare two presentations [R1][F10][X10].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and added 5.7pp of the 4.9% total growth [D382][D384][D342].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue but grew only 0.1%, contributing 0.1pp [D551][D552][D553].

FY2025 sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, and higher realized gas prices, partly offset by lower crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue rose 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Basic EPS fell 18.7% against net income's 13.6% decline as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D344][D343][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
FY2025 earnings fell on lower commodity prices, lower equity-affiliate earnings and higher exploration expense [P12].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
SG&A fell $265 million, mainly from the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D332][D298].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income, above the 2.07x window median [F59][F20][D333][D855].
Operating cash flow fell 1.6% in FY2025 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the Marathon Oil acquisition [D346][P6].
Free cash flow is only reported through FY2022, when it was $18.2 billion, a 23.1% margin [F73][D223].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, the window's highest capital intensity [D222][D228].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, with a 1.30x current ratio [D335][D357][F153].
Net cash cannot be computed after FY2020 because long-term debt is not reported after that year [R6][F157].
FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capital spending, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Dividends and buybacks of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [P31].
Revenue is recast in every year of the table, so margins and growth mix two presentations [R1][F1][X1].
Long-term debt is missing before FY2017 and after FY2020, so net cash and debt growth are unavailable across those breaks [R5][R6][X204][F157].
Short-term investments are missing in FY2021, so cash and investments that year omit them [R7][X183][X184].
Revenue declined 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices [R2][F8][D274][P47].
If net margin falls below the 17.9% window median again in FY2026, the FY2022 peak would look cyclical rather than structural [D831][F30].
Operating cash flow per dollar of net income above the 2.07x median would confirm the cash quality seen in FY2025 [D855][D333].
Dividends and buybacks above 46% of operating cash flow would exceed the FY2025 level and the 30% framework [P31].
